pr_body:
Previously, we did not support the DROP OWNED BY statement (#55381).
This commit adds partial support for DROP OWNED BY in the declarative
schema changer. Followup work is needed to support the CASCADE modifier.

Release note (sql change): Support `DROP OWNED BY`.

issue_context.title: sql: support DROP OWNED BY command
issue_context.body:
To facilitate dropping roles, we should support Postgres's DROP OWNED BY command. This drops all owned objects as well as any grants on objects not owned by the role.

Relevant Postgres docs:
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-drop-owned.html
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/role-removal.html

Epic CRDB-13664

Jira issue: CRDB-3673
comments: I'm tying up loose ends as I offboard this week and want to make sure that this issue is being tracked in the new SQL Experience board. I've removed myself from assigned so others will feel free to take it on. Thank you ✨

review_comments: User privileges are implicitly removed when dropping something, so you can remove this op altogether.
I believe `DROP OWNED BY` should revoke user privileges for the role(s) on objects that aren't owned, so we need this op to drop those privileges without dropping the entire objects.
Oh, right. In that case, you should update the rules to avoid emitting this op for dropped objects. Look for `op_rules.go`.

I think [this rule](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/2461c0883b2440997ed48130b183ba371f0490ef/pkg/sql/schemachanger/scplan/internal/rules/op_drop.go#L202-L239) should handle this, since user privileges are part of the descriptor.
